subject.title: sec (6/9): run user-defined scanners in an isolated working directory

question: Should Docker-mode user-defined scanners receive the target through a dedicated read-only mount and rewritten container path, preserving both scan functionality and isolation?
rationale: The PR changes the sandbox contract for arbitrary user commands. The repository needs an intentional, documented mapping boundary rather than relying on a host path or using an empty cwd as an implicit access policy.

options.title: Add a dedicated read-only target mount
options.body: Map only the requested local target into the container at a stable path, rewrite `{{target}}` to that path for Docker execution, and prove read succeeds while writes fail.

options.title: Keep Docker unsupported for local targets
options.body: Reject or clearly fail Docker-mode local user-defined scanner runs rather than silently launching a command that cannot inspect its target.

options.title: Pause this hardening step
options.body: Defer cwd isolation until the explicit sandbox-mount work can land with one coherent target-access contract.

recommendation.title: Add a dedicated read-only target mount
recommendation.body: Map only the requested local target into the container at a stable path, rewrite `{{target}}` to that path for Docker execution, and prove read succeeds while writes fail.
